phase1_categories.definition: Characteristics of RFID or of other technologies, in use at the firm or available on the market, as they bear on adoption or use: benefits over the status quo, cost and investment, complexity, fit with existing systems and data, read performance, data quality, standards.
phase1_categories.label: Technological context

phase1_categories.definition: Characteristics and resources of the adopting organisation: executive sponsorship, champions, structure and decision rights, skills and expertise, budget and staff time, redesign of work processes, size and slack.
phase1_categories.label: Organisational context

phase1_categories.definition: The setting in which the organisation operates: industry and market structure, competitors, customers, suppliers and value-chain partners (who tags, who pays, who mandates), technology suppliers and support, regulation and standards bodies.
phase1_categories.label: Environmental and interorganisational context

phase1_categories.definition: Descriptive information about the respondent, the organisation or the scope of the account: role, background, company, portfolio, which project, where and when. It explains nothing about adoption on its own: when the unit says why adoption advanced, stalled or failed, code TECH, ORG or ENV instead.
phase1_categories.label: Context of the account

prompt_template.codebook_intro: One code per line, as JSON with the fields code, label and definition. These {count} codes and NA are the only valid values.
prompt_template.footer:
1. Use ONLY the codes of the codebook, written exactly as listed. You may not create, merge or rename codes.
2. If no code applies, answer NA. NA is a valid and frequent answer; never force a code for the sake of completeness. NA is never combined with another code.
3. A unit may carry several codes.
4. Code what is SAID in the unit, not what you infer from the context of the interview. A unit that could not be coded on its own is coded NA.
5. Interviewer turns (speaker INT) are coded NA by default, unless the interviewer reports a fact from the field in that turn.
6. Write no comment, no justification and no memo.
7. Process EVERY unit listed under UNITS, in order, without omitting any: one entry per unit, no unit twice, no unit that is not listed.
prompt_template.header:
# Coding Studio: blind secondary coding

Detailed coding with concrete codes

## Role

You are a secondary coder on a qualitative study. You apply a closed codebook. You do not produce analysis, you do not build themes, and you do not interpret beyond the assignment of codes.

## Task

For each unit listed under UNITS, assign the code or codes of the codebook that apply. The codes name concrete mechanisms, such as a legal obligation, a customer requirement or a lack of skills. They are grouped by the context of the technology-organisation-environment (TOE) framework they belong to; the grouping is there for orientation only, and any code may apply to any unit.
prompt_template.units_intro: One unit per line, as JSON with the fields unit_id, speaker (INT = interviewer, RESP = respondent, any other label is the speaker label of the source), timestamp and text. Characters may appear as JSON escapes; read them as the characters they encode.
